summary: Healthcheck traffic and ephemeral worker fanout causing tenant 429s (burst-credit leakage)
description: Issue summary: Customer reports repeated 429 throttles for a dedicated tenant correlated with a scheduled healthcheck sweep and a transient increase in ephemeral worker count. Impact: Brightline ingestion pipelines report ~15% failed requests over a 20 minute window, causing missed SLAs for nightly processing. Environment: Dedicated pool in us-west, tenant on reserved GPUs, model redwood/gpt-lite-13b pinned for inference. Observation window: 2026-03-09 03:10 - 03:35 UTC.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer runs a parallel upload workflow with 80 short-lived ephemeral worker processes (ephemeral auth tokens) starting within a 30s window.
2) A scheduled healthcheck sweep (internal probe) for the customer's dedicated pool runs at the same minute (3:12 UTC).
3) The ingress edge proxies multiplex these sockets and the rate-controller attributes tokens to the tenant's burst pool which is near exhaustion.
4) Result: requests begin receiving 429s within 60-90s of the spike.
logs: 2026-03-09T03:12:11Z EDGE: signed-url-callback received for tenant T-98321, source ip x.x.x.x
2026-03-09T03:13:45Z CUSTOMER: "We see thousands of quick connect/disconnects from our worker pool and 20-30% of calls fail with 429"
investigation_notes: Support triage: initial hypothesis is double accounting when healthcheck probes and ephemeral auth refreshes coincide. Edge token-slicing may be attributing healthcheck increments to tenant burst pools without isolating probe traffic.
Observed: refill window shows expected interval but effective available burst credits drop faster than telemetry suggests (drift between edge and central metering ~10-15s).
Correlated dashboards: spike in 'ingress_ephemeral_token_count' aligns exactly with 429 uptick. No GPU saturation observed on dedicated nodes.
customer_communication: 2026-03-10 09:14 UTC - Support (Aisha): We received your report and are triaging. Can you confirm approximate worker fanout and whether you rotate ephemeral tokens per process?

2026-03-10 11:02 UTC - Customer (Brightline): We spawn 60-90 ephemeral workers per batch job, tokens are short-lived (120s) and rotated per worker. Healthcheck window is run by our ops at 03:12 UTC daily.

2026-03-11 08:44 UTC - Eng (Luca): We see edge-proxy incrementing 'probe' counters but some probes are on the same connection signature as user traffic; edge currently attributes refill events to the tenant. Investigating isolation patch.
current_hypothesis: Healthcheck and ephemeral worker token refreshes occur within the same refill epoch causing effective burst-credit leakage. Edge attribution logic is not fully isolating probe/healthcheck traffic from customer burst accounting when connections reuse signed URLs or share headers.
mitigation_steps: 1) Temporary workaround recommended to customer: stagger worker startup by 3-5s and avoid simultaneous ephemeral token refresh across all processes.
2) Support action: disable scheduled internal non-customer healthchecks for the impacted tenant's edge node for the next 48h while we validate attribution fix.
3) Engineering: prepare a hotfix to mark probe/healthcheck requests with a metadata flag so the rate-controller excludes them from tenant burst accounting.
4) Add console metric: 'probe_excluded_burst_leak' to detect similar events automatically.
resolution_notes: Temporary mitigation applied 2026-03-11 14:30 UTC: we disabled the overlapping internal probe for the customer's edge zone and asked Brightline to stagger worker spins. 429s dropped to baseline within 8 minutes. Engineering is preparing a small patch to ensure healthcheck/probe traffic is excluded from tenant burst accounting; target deploy to canary 2026-03-14. Follow-up: create a monitoring alert that fires when burst consumption spike coincides with probe_count>10.
postmortem_actions: - Engineering to ship probe-exclusion flag in rate-controller (PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rate-controller/pull/3812)
- Product to add guidance to dedicated onboarding docs recommending staggering ephemeral worker startups and configuring stagger in default SDK templates
- Support to add a diagnostic check into the onboarding health checklist to surface potential healthcheck/worker collisions
conclusion: Root cause: misattribution of probe/healthcheck traffic into tenant burst accounting combined with high ephemeral-worker fanout. Impact limited to customer's dedicated pool and resolved via probe disable + worker staggering. Permanent fix in review.
notes_for_follow_up: Verify canary metrics after PR merge: monitor 'burst_credit_delta', 'probe_excluded_burst_leak', and customer-side 429 rate for two rolling days post-deploy. Schedule follow-up with Brightline ops to confirm SDK stagger update.
